items.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999
items.q: My first record date, Kay [sic] Winding, or Kai as he was known later, Shelly Manne, Ed Safranski, and Allen...

ctx.x: Oh, he just wrote the parts individually.

What he did was, Neal Hefti was rooming with Shelly Manne the drummer. And Shelly used to complain because Neal didn’t know how to write a score, so he would whistle the arrangement, the entire arrangement from the introduction, chorus, modulation, out choruses, background choruses, everything he would whistle, each part, and after he finished the lead trumpet he would throw it on the floor and look at it, and harmonize it. [Whistles] He was whistling all night long, and Shelly used to call him “the whistler” —…
I guess so. You know it might have been an advantage for you that he didn’t get to the piano part, because he might have written something very difficult, if you weren’t a reader at the time.
